sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Round Rock?
sections.html:
A Round Rock homeowner is billed by a county tax office, and which county depends on where the house sits. The city straddles Williamson and Travis counties, and the city's own finance page says it has contracted with both tax offices to collect on its behalf.

Values come from the two appraisal districts, not from the city. The City of Round Rock property tax page lists the contacts for each side:

  • Williamson County Tax Office, 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, 512-943-1601.
  • Travis County Tax Office, 2433 Ridgepoint Dr., Austin, 512-854-9473.
  • Williamson Central Appraisal District, 625 F.M. 1460, Georgetown, 512-930-3787.
  • Travis Central Appraisal District, 850 E Anderson Lane, Austin, 512-834-9317.

Each county keeps a searchable tax database where you can type an address and see what every taxing unit on the parcel charges. Check which county your parcel is in before you call, because the two offices cannot see each other's accounts.

sections.h2: What is the Round Rock city tax rate?
sections.html:
The city's adopted rate for fiscal year 2025-2026 is 37.2000 cents per $100 of assessed value. The same page prints a median home value of $395,240 on the 2025 tax rolls and an estimated city tax bill of $1,470 for that median home.

That figure is only the city's slice. Your bill also carries the county, the school district and any special district, so the city number understates what you pay in total. The city also says it posts proposed rates each year under Tax Code Section 26.04, and that bills go out in October with delinquency starting February 1.

sections.h2: When are Round Rock property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in October, and the Comptroller says most owners must pay by January 31 to avoid delinquency on February 1. Your bill may allow a split payment, with the first half due by November 30 and the second half by June 30 of the next year.

Once a bill turns delinquent, a six percent penalty and one percent interest attach on February 1. The penalty grows one percent a month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent, and interest keeps running at one percent a month with no cap. A unit that hires a private collection attorney can add up to 20 percent more. The Comptroller's payment page lays out the full schedule.

Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, may pay in four installments instead. If you fall behind on a homestead, ask the collector whether a payment plan of up to 36 months is offered.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and caps lower a Round Rock tax bill?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption comes off the value that school districts tax, and the state requires a $140,000 exemption for a primary residence. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, get another $60,000 for school taxes. Cities and counties may add their own percentage exemption of up to 20 percent, so ask each office what it offers.

  • The appraised value of a homestead may rise no more than 10 percent a year, counted from the January 1 after you first qualify.
  • A school tax ceiling freezes the school tax on a 65-plus or disabled owner's home at the level of the year they first qualified.
  • Disabled veterans can receive a partial exemption scaled to their VA rating, and a total exemption on a homestead at 100 percent.
  • Applications are due by April 30, and the Comptroller's exemption guide lists the forms.

A buyer who closes after January 1 can claim the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller never received it. The Census counts 11.2 percent of Round Rock residents as 65 or older, so the freeze and the extra $60,000 matter to a real slice of owners.

sections.h2: How do I protest my Round Rock appraisal?
sections.html:
File a written protest with the appraisal review board by May 15, or within 30 days after your notice of appraised value was delivered if that is later. Notices for homesteads start going out around April 1, and hearings begin around mid-May.

If the board result still looks wrong, you can go to district court, binding arbitration, or, when the board value tops $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings. You usually need to pay the undisputed tax before the delinquency date to keep that appeal alive. Your file with the appraisal district is the first stop for comparable sales and the property record card.

sections.h2: What in Round Rock's history affects the age and risk of a house?
sections.html:
The town started near a round rock in the Brushy Creek crossing, and the post office was renamed Round Rock in 1854 because another Texas community already used Brushy. A newer downtown was platted in 1876 when the railroad arrived, and the city passed its first zoning ordinance in 1969.

The biggest change came in 1994, when Dell moved its world headquarters here and, in the city's own words, the deal produced a significant jump in the tax base. Growth in the mid-1980s ran 18 to 20 percent a year. Census figures show the population climbed 18.2 percent between April 2020 and July 2025.

Water has shaped some streets. The city's history timeline records flash flooding from Tropical Storm Hermine in September 2010, with 44 homes flooded, mostly in the Round Rock West subdivision and on Lake Creek Circle. A buyer or an inspector may ask about flood history on streets near Lake Creek or Brushy Creek, so keep repair records handy.

sections.h2: Do Round Rock short-term rentals face a separate tax?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's hotel occupancy FAQ says every short-term rental, meaning a stay under 30 consecutive days, owes 9 percent on monthly net receipts, made up of a 7 percent hotel tax and a 2 percent venue tax.

  • Registration costs $35 the first year and $25 to renew, due before January 1.
  • Each rental property registers on its own.
  • Returns are due by the last day of the month after the reporting month, even for a month with no rentals.
  • Late payments carry a penalty of 5, 10 or 15 percent depending on how late, plus 10 percent interest from day 61.
  • The city says Airbnb and Vrbo do not collect or remit this tax for owners.

If you plan to sell a house that has been rented short term, settle any unfiled returns first, because the account stays open until you file a closure form.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Round Rock property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1 and follows the house, so a buyer cannot get a clean title until the delinquent amount is paid. The person who owned the property on January 1 stays liable for that year's tax even after a sale.

In practice the title company asks the tax offices for a payoff figure and pays it from the sale proceeds at closing. Because Round Rock parcels fall under two counties, request the payoff from the right one and ask for any special district balance too. Deed recording happens at the county clerk, whose manual lists a $5.00 first-page fee and $4.00 for each added page, plus smaller state-set clerk fees.

Behind on Round Rock property tax and thinking about a quick sale? A written cash offer can show you the payoff and your net before you commit.

faqs.q: What is the Round Rock city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city lists an adopted rate of 37.2000 cents per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2025-2026. That covers only the city share, so your total bill also includes the county, the school district and any special district.

faqs.q: Which office do I pay if my Round Rock house is in two counties?
faqs.a: Pay the county tax office for the county where the parcel sits, either Williamson or Travis. The city says it contracts with both offices to collect its tax, so each parcel belongs to only one of them.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty if I pay Round Rock property tax after January 31?
faqs.a: Yes. On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added, and the penalty rises monthly to 12 percent by July 1. Interest continues at one percent a month, and a collection attorney's fee of up to 20 percent can follow.

faqs.q: Do I owe a hotel tax if I rent my Round Rock home on Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes. Round Rock charges 9 percent on net receipts from stays under 30 days, split between a 7 percent hotel tax and a 2 percent venue tax. You also register each property and file monthly returns, and the platforms do not remit it for you.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Round Rock house that still owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company gets a payoff figure from the county tax office. Ask for the balance in writing so you know your net before accepting an offer.
